reuse.why: Extends the existing getScheduledAmount and routes every server/shared site (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview, forecast, schedule-template, API model) through it, reusing getApproxNumberThreshold for the tolerance.

duplication.why: Removes five copies of the null/number/range midpoint dispatch in favour of the single helper and adds none.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, the API field is derived in api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal, and the list type change is in api-handlers types.

scope.why: Focused on amount resolution and the API field; the Balance.tsx touch is related but leaves the other client callers inconsistent.

maintainability.why: One definition of the expected amount; the positional boolean-then-op signature (getScheduledAmount(x, false, op)) is awkward, and client callers that omit op silently skip the approximate rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All amount resolution goes through getScheduledAmount; SchedulesTable, SchedulesListItem, MobileSchedulesPage and useScheduleEdit call it without op rather than bypassing it.

disguised_duplication.where: None; the inline copies were removed, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch; desktop-client callers other than Balance.tsx do not pass op, so the rule depends on each caller remembering it.
